title: Perception, capture, masking and secret detection
owns: app/main/perception/**, app/sidecar-host/**, sidecar/uia/ember_uia.cs, sidecar/atspi/**, app/remote/mask.ts and the remote desktop helper

findings.title: Screenshots throw RangeError when a never-look (or remote-surface) window lies to the left of the target window
findings.scenario: A password manager (KeePassXC, Bitwarden and 1Password are on the default never-look lists), or on Windows any Remote Desktop/WSLg window, sits to the left of the window Ember is looking at. Typical cases are the other monitor, or a half-screen tile with a gap, and the private window reaches the target's top edge row. Every perceive_window with image=true then rejects with 'RangeError: The value of "end" is out of range', so the tool call fails instead of returning a picture or a '(No screenshot: ...)' note. The model retries and burns steps. captureRect is given masks for every private window on the whole screen, not just ones overlapping the capture rectangle (perception/index.ts: `const mask = await this.privateWindows(stack)`). maskRect does `rgba.fill(0, (y*width+x0)*4, (y*width+x1)*4)` with x1 < 0, so the end offset is negative on rows near the top. app/remote/mask.ts:26 is a copy that has the guard `if (!(x1 > x0 && y1 > y0)) return;`, so only the local path is affected.
findings.evidence: Live, real sidecar + X11: target Electron window at x=500..1100,y=40, private window 'vault' at x=40..340,y=40..340, neverLook=['vault']: `perception.perceive({image:true,scope:'window',target:{pid}})` REJECTED with RangeError ... Received -640 (repro/exp22.test.ts). Without the never-look entry the same call returns a picture. Minimal: `maskRect(Buffer.alloc(100*50*4),100,50,{x:-60,y:0,width:20,height:10})` throws (repro/exp34.test.ts). Fuzz of 20000 random rects: 1258 throws, all left-of-image masks reaching the top rows (exp23, exp30). Model-based fuzz of Perception.perceive over 600 random layouts: 56 threw this error; the 544 that succeeded had every secret, private, cover and own-window region black. Re-run with a guarded copy of captureRect: 600/600 pass, window scope and screen scope (repro/exp24.test.ts, exp24b, exp35).
findings.fix: In maskRect (capture.ts) return early when the clipped rectangle is empty, as app/remote/mask.ts does: `if (!(x1 > x0 && y1 > y0)) return;` placed before the fill loops. Add unit tests for masks wholly left of, above, right of and below the image. Optionally also clip the mask list to the capture rect in captureRect.

findings.title: Windows UIA snapshot walks offscreen subtrees: long pages scrolled down read as empty, and screenshots of big pages are refused
findings.area: perception / large trees (Windows UIA bridge + sidecar host)
findings.scenario: On Windows, Chrome, Edge, Teams, Slack, Outlook-web and similar apps expose their whole page to UI Automation. Content above the viewport is reported IsOffscreen=true but with real bounds. The bridge's Walk.Visit goes pre-order and only prunes elements that are offscreen AND have no area (Props.Skipped, line 1744; PROTOCOL.md:300), so it descends into all offscreen content. The host asks for min(400*4, 4000)=1600 raw nodes per read and 6000 for the secret scan (reading.ts:28-34), counted over those offscreen nodes. Once the visible part is further than about 1600 elements into the tree, perceive_window lists only the window and the page container: nothing visible, with cut=['nodes'] and the text '(only the first 2 are listed. Scroll to the part you need...)'. That advice is wrong, because the part needed is on screen. Pages with more than 6000 accessible nodes (Gmail, GitHub PR diffs, long articles) also make secret_fields incomplete, so every screenshot is declined with 'the window is too big for Ember to check all of it for password fields'. The Linux sidecar and the macOS provider prune by what shows, so Windows is the outlier. host tree.ts:118 then discards every offscreen node and its subtree anyway, so descending into them is wasted work.
findings.evidence: Reproduced on the real host code with the repo's FakeProvider, which implements the bridge's documented semantics (offscreen-with-bounds elements are listed and counted): 25 visible links preceded by N offscreen links. N=300 and 1200: all 25 listed. N=1700 and 3000: 0 of 25 listed, 2 nodes, truncated=true, cut=['nodes'] (repro/exp39.test.ts). C# source read: Walk.Visit recurses into every child returned by Children(), which filters only Props.Skipped, i.e. offscreen with no area. No test in the repo exercises a long or scrolled page on Windows (the benches are small WinForms/WPF windows). Not run on a real Windows desktop.
findings.fix: In the bridge, do not descend into an element whose IsOffscreen is true (keep listing the node itself, with its flag). The host throws those subtrees away anyway (tree.ts:118, reading.ts:303), so behaviour is unchanged except that the budget goes to what shows. Alternatively order children on-screen first for every node, not only when there are more than 200. Add a Windows integration test with a few thousand offscreen elements before the visible ones, and word the 'nodes' note differently when the cut was in offscreen content.

findings.title: Windows/macOS host has no protection for names that contain the value of a secret field the read didn't list
findings.area: secrets in text sent to the model (sidecar host)
findings.scenario: Chromium (Chrome, Edge, Electron, Chromium-based macOS apps) names a table cell, row, <label> or section after the values of the fields inside it; I confirmed live that Blink does this: section 'Card number 4111 1111 1111 1111', table cell 'PIN 4821'. On Linux the sidecar withholds such names even when the field itself is not in the read (scrolled partly out of view, or past the node limit) through unlisted_secrets/name_says_secret (ember_atspi.py:1855). The TS host only compares names with the values of secret fields it listed (Secrets.redact -> withheldIds over `hidden`). Fields that are offscreen are dropped in buildNodes (tree.ts:118) before their value is ever considered. So a checkout form scrolled so that the card row is cut at the viewport edge, with the label or cell still partly visible, puts the card number into perceive_window's output on Windows (and at_point/read_element, which use the same remembered values). The Linux tests cover exactly this case (PERC9-1/PERC9-3); there is no TS-host test or doc for it.
findings.evidence: FakeProvider + real Host: DataItem named 'Card number 4111 1111 1111 1111' (partly visible) containing an offscreen Edit with that value: read_window lists `table cell name='Card number 4111 1111 1111 1111'` (repro/exp36.test.ts). The same page on Linux through the real sidecar names the container with the value (repro/exp37.test.ts). grep for unlisted/PERC9 in app/sidecar-host, test/unit/sidecar-host-*.ts and the docs finds nothing. Not run on Windows or macOS; whether UIA/AX expose the same container names there depends on Chromium's cross-platform naming, which is the basis for the finding.
findings.fix: In buildNodes, for fields skipped because they are offscreen (or cut), still evaluate isSecret and put their raw values into `hidden` (the snapshot already carries `value` for offscreen elements with bounds) so Secrets.redact/withheldIds withholds the listed containers that say them. For fields the read cut off by maxNodes, withhold names of the last listed element and its ancestors, as the Python stop-set does. Add tests mirroring PERC9-1/PERC9-3.

findings.title: Secret-label vocabulary misses seed/recovery phrases, '6-digit code' style one-time codes and non-English reveal toggles
findings.scenario: Fields are protected by their name or label matching SECRET_WORDS (mirrored in ember_atspi.py SECRET_WORDS, kept equal by a unit test). The lists say they cover one-time codes and keys, yet they do not match: 'Seed phrase', 'Recovery phrase', 'Mnemonic' (a wallet restore screen); 'Enter the 6-digit code', '6-digit code', 'Authenticator code', 'SMS code', 'Login code', 'Sign-in code', 'Access code', 'Activation code', 'Unlock code', 'Pass code' (every 2FA prompt); 'Security token', 'Master key', 'SSH key'. A wallet seed phrase or a 2FA code typed into such a field is then returned in perceive_window's text and shown unmasked in the screenshot, so it reaches the cloud model. 'Secret Recovery Phrase' and 'Verification code' do match, which shows the intent. Separately, the reveal-toggle verb list (REVEAL, elements.ts:153) lacks ko, da, no, hu, ro, el, vi, id, ar, he and th, so an unlabelled revealed password field beside '비밀번호 표시', 'Vis adgangskode', 'Jelszó megjelenítése', 'Afișează parola' and the like is not treated as secret (the English, German, French, Japanese, Chinese and Russian toggles are).
findings.evidence: Real Electron page through the real sidecar and Perception.perceive(image:true): `entry "Seed phrase" (editable, multi line) ... text="LEAKSEED apple banana cherry"` and `entry "Enter the 6-digit code" (editable) ... text="LEAK654321"` are printed and not marked secret, while `Enter secret` is secret; green text from those fields remains in the JPEG (repro/exp1.test.ts). isSecretLabel() over 80 labels: plain for Seed phrase, Recovery phrase, Mnemonic, 6-digit code, Authenticator code, Login code, Access code, SMS code, Sign-in code, Security token. secretIds() with a nameless entry beside toggles in 17 languages: only the 6 listed above flag it (repro/exp12.test.ts). test/fixtures/secret-labels.json has none of these phrases.
findings.fix: Add to both lists (keep them identical): `(seed|recovery|backup|secret recovery) phrases?`, `mnemonics?`, `(\\d+|six|four)[- ]digit codes?`, `(authenticator|authentication|sms|text message|login|log-in|sign-in|access|activation|unlock|mfa|passcode|pass code) codes?`, `(security|session|refresh|id) tokens?`, `(master|signing|ssh) keys?`; extend REVEAL with the missing languages' verbs. Add rows to secret-labels.json (secret and plain: 'Discount code', 'Postcode' must stay plain).

findings.title: Remote desktop helper has no Xlib error handler: a window closing between two X calls kills it
findings.area: sidecar/helper crash recovery (SSH remote desktop child)
findings.scenario: The desktop child is plain Node and uses x11.ts (stack(), activeWindow(), clientWindows(), describe()) and hands/input.ts. Each lists windows, then queries each one with XGetWindowAttributes, XGetWindowProperty and XGetGeometry. If a window is destroyed in between (a menu, tooltip or dialog closing right after Ember's click), the X server sends BadWindow and Xlib's default error handler calls exit(1). The helper dies, serve reports 'Ember's desktop helper on <host> stopped', and the task loses the remote screen until the PC asks again, possibly with a new consent prompt at the remote console. Electron's main process is protected (Chromium installs a handler) and the desk helper explicitly calls XSetErrorHandler (desk/agent-process.ts:26 'A window that closes between two calls (BadWindow) must not end the helper'), but the remote child does not. The race window is small, so this is rare in normal use but not impossible.
findings.evidence: Plain Node + koffi: `XGetWindowAttributes(dpy, bogusWindow, buf)` prints 'X Error of failed request: BadWindow' and exits 1, while the same call in Electron 44's main process returns 0 and survives. The real openX11().stack()/activeWindow() loop in plain Node, run beside a GTK script that creates and destroys popup windows rapidly, exited with BadWindow in 3 of 3 runs within 12 to 447 requests. With one tooltip-like popup every 400 ms it survived 200 calls over 60 s (repro/hammer.ts, hammer2.ts; xerr/plain.js).
findings.fix: Install a no-op XSetErrorHandler once when the child starts (move ignoreXErrors from desk/agent-process.ts into x11.ts and call it from openX11 when process.versions.electron is unset, or call it first thing in runDesktopChild). Ideally also have the child return null for a window that disappeared.

findings.title: perceive() takes an unscanned whole-screen screenshot when the requested window is gone or busy
findings.scenario: perceive({image:true, scope:'window', target}) computes `windowScope = scope === 'window' && !!(seen.window || seen.x11Window)`. When the target window has closed, never matched, or its app is hung (read returns window:null), windowScope is false and the code carries on to capture the entire screen (rect = screenBounds()). No secret fields are scanned (the `if (seen.window)` block is skipped), only never-look/own windows are masked, and the text says 'The focused window exposes no accessibility information; use the screenshot.' Today the Worker discards the image because it returns fail() when !p.window, so nothing reaches the model. But the capture still happens: on macOS it shows the recording indicator, a hung app costs about 3.6 s, and for SSH remotes the whole remote screen is PNG-encoded and shipped over the link (serve.ts perceive) before the PC drops it. One refactor of the Worker, or any new caller, would send an unmasked full-screen picture to the model on an operation that promises a window.
findings.evidence: Target Electron app killed, or a nonexistent title: perceive returned capture rect {0,0,1600,900} with the other window's green card-number text still in it (190 green px) and window=false (repro/exp14.test.ts). With the target process SIGSTOPped: capture=true, rect full screen, 64 green px, busy=true, 3.6 s (repro/exp13.test.ts). worker.ts:1605-1613 shows the Worker dropping it.
findings.fix: In perceive(): if opts.scope === 'window' && !windowScope, return noShot('the window can't be found (it may have closed or its app isn't answering)') before any capture. Keep whole-screen capture for scope 'screen' only.

findings.title: read_window gives no 'page still loading' signal when a browser document isn't handed over yet
findings.platforms: linux (Chromium/Electron via AT-SPI); Windows UIA likely similar
findings.scenario: A very large page, or the first read after a Chromium app turns on accessibility, shows a 'document web' with childCount 0 and 0x0 extents until the browser has built its tree. scan_fields knows this (not_ready -> cut 'loading' -> secret_fields busy), but walk()/read_window ignore it. The read returns just the window frame and the browser's menu bar or toolbar, with truncated false and busy false, so perceive_window and describe_screen present an apparently complete window that has no page content. The model may say the page is empty or the window has only a menu bar. Only a screenshot request is told 'the app is busy ... try again in a moment', and a very big page stayed in this state for the whole 55 s I watched.
findings.evidence: Electron page with 9000 links: pyatspi says `document found; childCount= 0 extents= {width:0,height:0} not_ready= True` for every poll up to 53 s, while read_window returned 6 nodes (frame, menu bar, 4 buttons), trunc=false, busy=undefined, and secret_fields returned complete=false busy=true each time (repro/exp19.test.ts, exp5, exp6). A 1800-link page of the same shape read normally.
findings.fix: In walk(), when a document role is not_ready, call budget.cut_short('loading'); pass 'loading' through ReadWindowResult.cut and map it in Perception.read/notes() to '(The page is still loading, so its content isn't listed yet. Try again in a moment.)' instead of the 'depth'/'nodes' texts. Do the same in the TS host for a Document with no children and no area.

findings.title: An app's own override-redirect popups are drawn in window screenshots without being scanned for secret fields
findings.platforms: linux (X11); Windows popups by the same rule
findings.scenario: coveringRects deliberately does not black out the target app's own override-redirect windows (menus, lists, tooltips) because they are 'part of what the worker looks at'. Their accessibility trees are not read for secrets, though: read_window walks only the target frame, and `others` lists only active or modal windows by name. A popup holding a field named 'Card number' or 'Login code' with its text visible (a GTK popover or entry-completion window, or a Firefox-style doorhanger or autofill panel; I did not test Firefox) therefore appears unmasked in the 'window with numbered marks' image. It is not in the text either, so the model sees an unlisted secret.
findings.evidence: GTK3 app with a main window plus a POPUP-type window over it containing Entries named 'Card number' (4111 1111 1111 1111) and 'Login code': X stack shows the popup as overrideRedirect=true with the same pid; perceive of the main window returned a capture with 836 green pixels from the popup's text and no node for it in the read (repro/exp20.test.ts). I did not find a concrete production popup that carries a full secret; Chromium/Firefox popup behaviour is unverified.
findings.fix: When the stack has same-pid override-redirect windows overlapping the target, scan their accessibility frames with secret_fields (they are top-level frames of the same app) and mask the secrets, or black out the whole popup when it can't be scanned. Cheap fallback: treat a same-pid popup as a cover if it overlaps the window and isn't a menu/tooltip by size.

findings.title: Remote viewers and VM windows are not masked as remote surfaces on Linux and macOS
findings.scenario: REMOTE_SURFACE is null for Linux and macOS, so only Windows blacks out Remote Desktop/WSLg windows (README and DEVELOPING.md 10.8 say so and list Hyper-V, VNC, TeamViewer and Citrix as not covered, but only for Windows). On a RHEL 8 workstation a window of virt-manager/virt-viewer, GNOME Boxes, Remmina or VNC Viewer (macOS: Screen Sharing, Microsoft Remote Desktop, Parallels, VMware Fusion, UTM) shows a whole guest or remote desktop that accessibility cannot see into. A window screenshot of it can contain the guest's password manager, login forms and revealed passwords, with none of the never-look or secret-field masking applying. Nothing in the docs tells Linux or macOS users that these are exposed, and the default never-look lists don't include them.
findings.evidence: Code reading: remote-surface.ts REMOTE_SURFACE = { linux: null, win32: /^(msrdc|mstsc|...)/i, darwin: null }; Perception.remoteSurfaces() returns [] when no isRemoteSurface is passed (main.ts passes remoteSurfaceCheck(platform.os), undefined for Linux and macOS). DEVELOPING.md:700-702 'Linux and macOS are unaffected'.
findings.fix: Add Linux/macOS rows for the common viewers (virt-manager, virt-viewer, gnome-boxes, remmina, vinagre, vncviewer, krdc, parallels, vmware, utm, screensharing, microsoft remote desktop) and black them out like Windows' clients, or at least state the gap in the README and doctor output.

findings.title: Missing or revoked Screen Recording on macOS is reported to the user and model as 'the window is off screen'
findings.scenario: Screen Recording not allowed (first run, never granted) or revoked later (also macOS 15's monthly re-approval declined). capture.ts returns null at once without asking macOS, so perceive() ends at `noShot("the window is off screen, or the screen couldn't be captured safely")`. The worker hears '(No screenshot: the window is off screen, or the screen couldn't be captured safely.)' and tells the user that, or retries; nobody mentions Screen Recording, there is no 'Open settings' action, and the handle still says 'Ready'. Because Ember never touches desktopCapturer without the permission, macOS never prompts either: the user only learns by finding the Setup check. The Accessibility and Input Monitoring refusals, by contrast, name the System Settings pane (ax-darwin-read.ts:54, darwin/input.ts:30,51).
findings.evidence: app/main/platform/darwin/capture.ts:50-56 (null without permission, no reason); app/main/perception/index.ts:405-409, 507; PlatformWords (app/shared/words.ts) has no 'no screenshot because of permission' field; windows.screenRecording() exists but perceive() doesn't ask it.
findings.fix: Add a platform word (e.g. screenshotsBlocked: "Ember doesn't have the Screen Recording permission (System Settings › Privacy & Security › Screen Recording)") and have perceive() use it when the window system reports no screen access. Raise a bubble/notice with an 'Open settings' action the first time per run.

findings.title: macOS without Screen Recording (never granted, or revoked while running): screenshots fail with "the window is off screen"
findings.scenario: A user who skips or later revokes Screen Recording (a common first-run choice, and the setup row is only a warning) asks Ember something that needs a picture. captureRect() returns null at once (darwin/capture.ts:56, `if (!allowed) return null`) and perceive() answers "(No screenshot: the window is off screen, or the screen couldn't be captured safely.)". The model then tells the user the window is off screen. Only the settings window's Screen Recording row, or `--doctor`, mentions the permission, so a user who never opens them is never told.
findings.evidence: Read the path: darwin/windows.ts capture() -> captureRect() returns null without the permission -> captureRect in perception/capture.ts returns null -> perception/index.ts:507 uses the generic note. grep for "Screen Recording" outside platform/darwin, environment.ts and the vocabulary returns nothing in perception or agent code, and PlatformWords has no field for this reason.
findings.fix: Add a PlatformWords field (for example noScreenshot) or let the window system's capture report why. On macOS the note should say "Ember doesn't have the Screen Recording permission (System Settings > Privacy & Security)" and the conductor could mention it once.
